set.typical_award_size: The 2024 Housing Opportunities Overlay Manual allows 100% affordable rental or ownership projects, emergency shelters, multi-service centers and low-barrier navigation centers by right in the C1, C2, CN, MX, M1, R2, R3 and R4 districts of unincorporated Orange County, approved through an administrative Affordable Housing Permit with no public hearing (the permit process also applies to projects at least 20% affordable in those districts). Qualified projects must be 100% affordable to low and very low income households (at or below 80% AMI), with 70% low income and at least 30% very low income units, a minimum density of 30 units per acre and generally at least 16 units. Density bonus follows Government Code 65915; on-menu incentives include side, front and rear setback reductions, up to 10 feet and one additional story of height, and a lot consolidation density incentive up to 45% total. The County NOFA's Attachment J lists eligible sites. No county inclusionary housing ordinance or in-lieu fee.

set.typical_award_size: Formula PLHA entitlement, not offered to developers. Santa Ana received $14,360,783 over PLHA Rounds 1 to 4; Round 4 (FY 2023-24 NOFA, HCD Contract 20-PLHA-15193) was a $2,403,595 grant recognized by Council on November 19, 2024. Round 1 paid Santa Ana Navigation Center tenant improvements, Rounds 2 and 3 paid for purchase of that property, and Round 4 funds Navigation Center operating costs and homeless services ($2,283,415 to a subagent, $120,180 staff). The 2021-2029 Housing Element lists PLHA as a funding source for emergency shelter and permanent supportive housing programs.
eligible_project_detail: PSH listed as an eligible Housing Element use but no allocation to development found
set.next_deadline: No developer round. Allocations to date are committed to the Santa Ana Navigation Center; confirm with the Housing Division whether any future PLHA year will be set aside for development.
set.cycle_notes: Annual HCD formula allocation to the City; City programs it internally rather than through a developer NOFA.
set.layering_notes: Santa Ana is an HCD PLHA entitlement separate from the County Urban County allocation. All four rounds so far went to the Santa Ana Navigation Center (tenant improvements, property purchase, operations), so developers should not count on City PLHA as gap money unless a later five-year plan amendment shifts funds to rental production. Sources: November 19, 2024 staff report with HCD award letter (Laserfiche WebLink doc 224140) and the September 2022 Housing Element.

reason: November 19, 2024 staff report shows all PLHA rounds funded the Navigation Center, so the developer-facing description and project types were corrected.

set.typical_award_size: In-lieu fees are deposited in the City's affordable housing fund and used for projects implementing the Housing Element needs assessment or serving low, very low and extremely low income households; the fee is charged per market-rate unit under a Council-approved formula, determined at building permit, and has not been updated since 2011 (a legacy $17,000 per unit rate applied only to pre-2007 Irvine Business Complex filings). A May 2026 Draft Affordable Housing and In-Lieu Fee Analysis was released August 10, 2026; staff recommends keeping the existing formula with updated inputs. Finance Commission reviewed it October 19, 2026; Planning Commission and Council hearings are not yet scheduled. Fund balance and any developer allocation process are not published.
set.next_deadline: No NOFA located as of November 8, 2026. In-lieu fee update pending Planning Commission and City Council hearings (dates TBD). Ask Community Development (cd@cityofirvine.org) for the fund balance and whether a developer round is planned.
set.layering_notes: Because most Irvine builders provide units on-site or through credits, the in-lieu fund is smaller than Santa Ana's; its visible use is land and loans to Irvine Community Land Trust projects (Salerno, Parc Derian, Doria, Alegre, Sage Park) which then take LIHTC, HOME, OCHFT and County MHSA money. Public funds trigger state prevailing wage. set.layering_notes: Reclassified from other to regulatory requirement: the credits program is part of the Chapter 2-3 inclusionary procedure (15% requirement, 5% each extremely low or very low, low and moderate) and is a compliance-trading mechanism, not a public subsidy. For a 100% affordable developer it can still be a revenue source: excess units earn credits (for example 2.0 credits per ownership unit sold to lower income buyers, 1.6 extremely low or very low credits per qualifying rental unit, one credit releasing 19 market-rate units) that can be sold to market-rate builders. Confirm with the City how many credits are outstanding and the recent trading range. Read on the zoneomics mirror because the City-linked Municode page is Cloudflare-blocked; the City in-lieu fee page (cityofirvine.gov/node/94569) confirms the 15% requirement and menu options.

reason: Credits are a trading mechanism inside the inclusionary ordinance, so regulatory requirement fits better than other; code text re-read and matches the record.
